words.meaning: a long time with no rain, so plants cannot grow

words.meaning: water covering land that is usually dry
words.example: The flood damaged many homes near the river.

words.meaning: collecting crops from the fields when they are ready

words.meaning: from the sun, or using energy from the sun
words.example: They put solar panels on the roof of their house.

grammar.title: First conditional and future time clauses
grammar.explanation:
We use the **first conditional** for real future possibilities.

The rule is: **if** + present simple, **will** / **won't** + verb. If we recycle more, we will have less pollution.

Never use **will** after **if**. We say: If the drought ends, we will be happy. Not: if the drought will end.

**Unless** means **if not**. The wildlife will disappear unless we protect it.

We also use the present tense, not the future, after **when**, **as soon as**, **until**, **before**, and **after**. We say: I will call you when I arrive. Not: when I will arrive.
examples: *If we recycle* more, *we will have* less pollution in our city. (first conditional)
*If the drought ends*, farmers *will get* a good harvest. (first conditional)
The panda *will disappear* *unless* people protect it. (unless = if not)
*Unless* we use solar energy, pollution *will grow*. (unless)
I *will visit* the national park *when* I *have* time. (present tense after when)
We *will stay* inside *until* the flood *goes* down. (present tense after until)
